findings.quote: These formulas also work for an angle from $0^\circ$ to $360^\circ$, and the signs come out correctly by themselves. Why: for an angle $\theta$ over $90^\circ$, $V\cos\theta$ is the horizontal part of the arrow.
findings.problem: This paragraph in Resolving a Vector into Components has six sentences: the any-angle claim, the reason, the left-pointing arrow, the 150 degree example, the unit-circle pointer and the measured-from-vertical rule. The guide allows one to three short sentences per paragraph. A few other paragraphs run to four very short sentences (for example the resultant and tip-to-tail paragraphs), but this one is the clear breach. It is style only: the teaching is correct and complete.
